action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). <?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## pinecone-v2
Pinecone is a vector database that provides AI
tools and applications with fast, scalable, and flexible vector search.

Instructions for usage:
- Always search the documentation before attempting to explain or write code for
Pinecone. When writing code, always refer to examples from the documentation. Do
not make assumptions about usage. Always use the latest SDK version.

- If the code uses an index or namespace, make sure you use the correct names I
have configured or help me create new ones.

- Always use a consistent schema for records in an index. Do not use different
field names in the same index. Always put the text content in the field named in
the index's "fieldMap". Do not use objects as field values. Do not include a
"metadata" field.

- When searching for records, make sure to use a query that accurately reflects
my needs. Only use a filter if you are sure it will help me find the records I
need. Craft filters knowing the schema of the data in the index.

- If you receive an error, read the error response to understand what went
wrong. "MCP error -32602" means your input was wrong. Correct your input by
following the instructions carefully.

1	# Trial class booking: design
2	
3	Date: 2026-10-20 · Status: approved 2026-10-21
4	
5	## 1. What this is and why
6	
7	Codeyoung's take-home assignment: a web app where a parent books a free trial class and the system
8	assigns an available mentor. Parents are in the US or UK; mentors are in India. Both sides get the
9	class link and the time in their own local time.
10	
11	The assignment is graded on product and UX, on how carefully capacity, availability, time zones, DST
12	and concurrency are handled, and on architecture, code quality, tests, AI usage and documentation.
13	The two hard parts are **concurrency** (never overbook a mentor) and **dates and times** (never show
14	a misleading time). Everything else stays deliberately small: "a working, understandable,
15	customer-friendly solution over unnecessary complexity".
16	
17	### The numbers
18	
19	| | |
20	|---|---|
21	| Mentors | 10, all in India today |
22	| Demand | about 20 parents a day |
23	| Cap | at most 2 trial classes per mentor per day |
24	
25	10 × 2 = 20 classes a day against about 20 parents a day, so capacity equals demand. "Fully booked" is
26	a normal state, not a rare edge case, and the full/empty screens get real design.
27	
28	### Calendar facts this design leans on
29	
30	On the design date, Tue 20 Oct 2026:
31	
32	- UK and Ireland clocks go back on **Sun 25 Oct 2026** at 01:00 UTC (BST → GMT, Irish IST → GMT).
33	- US clocks go back on **Sun 1 Nov 2026** at 2:00 AM local time, zone by zone.
34	- India has no DST: IST is always UTC+5:30.
35	
36	A 14-day booking window opened that day spans both changes. That is why the window is 14 days and
37	not Codeyoung's 7.
38	
39	With the real clock, both changes have left the window by 1 Nov, and the next one (US, Sun 14 Mar
40	2027) only enters it around 28 Feb 2027. Reviewers will likely run the app in between, so the app has
41	a demo clock (`DEMO_NOW`, section 7) that shows the DST behaviour live at any time.
42	
43	## 2. Goals, non-goals, anti-goals
44	
45	### Goals
46	
47	- A parent books a trial in three short steps and always sees times in their own zone, with the zone
48	  abbreviation and city.
49	- The system assigns the mentor. A mentor is never double-booked for an hour and never has more than
50	  2 active classes on one day in **the mentor's own time zone**, even when many parents book at the
51	  same moment.
52	- Full days, full hours and "just taken" each have a clear, friendly state that offers the nearest
53	  alternatives.
54	- The parent and the mentor each get an email in their own time zone, sent only after the booking
55	  commits.
56	- One `docker compose up` migrates, seeds (including some pre-booked classes) and serves everything.
57	- Heavy, real tests on concurrency and time handling: real Postgres, fixed clocks, and tests that are
58	  shown to fail when the protection is removed.
59	- Reviewers can see the clock changes in the running app whenever they run it (demo clock).
60	
61	### Non-goals (not built; say so in the README)
62	
63	- Accounts, login, admin screens.
64	- Cancelling or rescheduling from the app. The data model has `cancelled_at`, so only active
65	  bookings count, but there is no cancel button or endpoint.
66	- Phone/OTP verification, course or grade selection, subject-based mentor matching.
67	- Mentor time off or holiday exceptions.
68	- Calendar invites (.ics), SMS, reminders.
69	- 30-minute start times or overlapping classes.
70	- "One free trial per family" limits.
71	- Per-reader locale formatting. Everyone gets one display style (section 7).
72	- Marketing content: no pitch column, trust badges, reviews or FAQ.
73	- Guaranteed email delivery (outbox pattern).
74	
75	### Anti-goals (a failure even if it works)
76	
77	- A time shown anywhere without its zone context, or a fixed UTC offset assumed for a US/UK zone.
78	- Overbooking under concurrency: a double-booked hour, or a third class in a mentor's day.
79	- Server output that depends on the host machine's time zone.
80	- An email for a booking that didn't commit, or a booking lost because email failed.
81	- Showing a booking as made before the server confirms it.
82	- A demo clock that isn't clearly labelled as one.
83	- Concurrency tests that still pass with the lock removed.
84	- Bloat: component libraries, ORMs, date libraries, a router library.
85	
86	## 3. Constraints
87	
88	- The repository is public, and the AI transcript is published with it as `TRANSCRIPT.md`. No secrets
89	  beyond the repo's own (the Postgres password in `docker-compose.yml` is fine).
90	- Submission needs `README.md` (install, configure, run, test, API docs, assumptions, architecture
91	  notes), `TRANSCRIPT.md`, seed data and environment-variable instructions.
92	- Commit messages and PR titles are entirely lowercase.
93	- Every container runs with `TZ=UTC`.
94	- Codeyoung's look: Satoshi font, accent `#FBB600` with dark text, their corner radii and sizes.
95	
96	## 4. Stack and layout
97	
98	- **Docker Compose**, three services plus a test service:
99	  - `db`: Postgres 17 (`postgres:17-alpine`), healthcheck with `pg_isready`.
100	  - `mailpit`: catches all email. UI at `http://localhost:8025`, SMTP on `mailpit:1025`.
101	  - `app`: `depends_on: db: condition: service_healthy` (and `mailpit`). On start it runs
102	    migrations, then the seed, then serves the API and the built React app on
103	    `http://localhost:3000`. One origin: no CORS, no nginx.
104	  - `test`: same image built with dev dependencies, under a compose profile so `up` never starts it.
105	    `docker compose run --rm test` runs the whole suite against the `db` service.
106	  - All services set `TZ=UTC`.
107	- **Backend**: Node 24, Express 5, TypeScript, Zod, `pg` (node-postgres) with plain SQL.
108	  - Express 5 forwards rejected promises from async handlers to error middleware, so there is no
109	    async wrapper.
110	  - The server runs its TypeScript directly with Node's built-in type stripping, and `tsc --noEmit`
111	    only typechecks. That means erasable syntax only: no `enum`, no namespaces, no parameter
112	    properties, and `.ts` extensions in relative imports. If type stripping misbehaves in the Docker
113	    image, fall back to a plain `tsc` build step. Don't reach for a third runner.
114	  - Migrations are numbered `.sql` files (`migrations/001_init.sql`, …) plus a ~20-line runner. The
115	    runner holds a Postgres advisory lock, applies files not yet recorded in `schema_migrations`
116	    (each in its own transaction) and records them.
117	- **Frontend**: React with Vite, built to static files that Express serves, with an SPA fallback for
118	  non-`/api` paths.
119	  - TanStack Query for all server data. No fetching inside `useEffect`.
120	  - Tailwind CSS v4 through `@tailwindcss/vite`. No component library.
121	  - The whole palette lives in one `@theme` block (section 10), and nothing else hard-codes a colour.
122	- **Email**: nodemailer to Mailpit.
123	- **Tests**: Vitest, plus supertest for HTTP.
124	- **One package** (one `package.json`) with `src/server`, `src/web` and `src/shared`.
125	  - `src/shared/time.ts` is imported by both server and browser, so the UI and the emails format time
126	    with the same code.
127	  - Libraries only the browser bundle needs (React, TanStack Query, Tailwind, Vite) are dev
128	    dependencies, because they are compiled away. The runtime image then only installs Express, `pg`,
129	    Zod and nodemailer.
130	
131	Suggested layout (keep files few; split only when a file gets unwieldy):
132	
133	```
134	docker-compose.yml  Dockerfile  package.json  tsconfig.json  vite.config.ts  index.html
135	migrations/001_init.sql
136	src/shared/time.ts                 + time.test.ts
137	src/server/main.ts                 migrate → seed → listen
138	src/server/app.ts                  express app factory: routes + error middleware
139	src/server/db.ts                   pool + migration runner
140	src/server/slots.ts                pure slot building          + slots.test.ts
141	src/server/bookings.ts             the booking transaction     + bookings.test.ts
142	src/server/email.ts                pure rendering + sending    + email.test.ts
143	src/server/seed.ts
144	src/server/api.test.ts             HTTP behaviour via supertest
145	src/web/main.tsx  App.tsx  index.css
146	src/web/BookingPage.tsx  ConfirmationPage.tsx  MentorsPage.tsx
147	src/web/hooks.ts                   useTimeZone, useSlots, useBookSlot
148	src/web/booking.ts                 reducer + pure helpers      + booking.test.ts
149	```
150	
151	`createApp({ pool, clock, mailer })` takes its dependencies, so tests pass a fixed clock, a test pool
152	and a fake or broken mailer. In production `clock` is the real clock, or the demo clock when
153	`DEMO_NOW` is set (section 7).
154	
155	## 5. Domain rules
156	
157	- **Mentors** have an IANA time zone and weekly working hours written in their own time zone.
158	- **Classes** are 60 minutes and start on the hour in UTC. Classes never overlap. US and UK zones are
159	  whole hours from UTC, so parents see on-the-hour times; mentors in India see half-past times
160	  (8:30 PM IST).
161	- **Booking window**: a class can start at the earliest 2 hours from now and at the latest 14 days
162	  from now.
163	- **Eligible mentor** for an hour:
164	  - the mentor's working hours cover the whole class,
165	  - the mentor has no active booking at that hour,
166	  - and the mentor has fewer than 2 active bookings on that calendar day in the mentor's own time zone.
167	- **Assignment**: among eligible mentors, pick the one with the fewest active bookings that day, then
168	  the lowest id.
169	- **The daily cap** counts the calendar day in **the mentor's own time zone**. Write it that way in
170	  code, comments and README, never as "IST". All mentors are in India today so the result is the
171	  same, and it keeps working if a mentor is ever elsewhere.
172	  - Example (also a test): a Los Angeles parent's Mon 26 Oct, 6:00 PM PDT is Tue 27 Oct, 6:30 AM in
173	    Kolkata. The parent sees it under Monday, and it counts toward the mentor's Tuesday.
174	- **Active** booking means `cancelled_at IS NULL`. Every rule above counts only active bookings.
175	
176	## 6. Concurrency
177	
178	Postgres enforces both limits. The mental model is a turnstile on the mentor's row: bookings for the
179	same mentor take turns, and bookings for different mentors run in parallel.
180	
181	```
182	Mentor 7 already has 1 class that day. Two parents book 15:00Z and 16:00Z at once.
183	
184	T1: lock 7 → free at 15:00? yes → 1 < 2? yes → INSERT → COMMIT (lock released)
185	T2: lock 7 → (waits for T1) → free at 16:00? yes → 2 < 2? no → ROLLBACK → try next mentor
186	```
187	
188	### The booking function: `bookSlot(pool, input, now, hooks?)`
189	
190	1. Input is already validated (section 8). The requested time must be on the UTC hour and inside the
191	   booking window. If it isn't, return `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`.
192	2. Work out candidate mentors in plain JavaScript: their working hours cover the class. Sort them by
193	   that day's active count, then by id. This pre-check only sets the order. It is not trusted.
194	3. For each candidate, run one short transaction at Postgres's default READ COMMITTED:
195	   1. `SELECT id FROM mentors WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE`. This is the turnstile.
196	   2. Free at that hour? Check for an active booking with this `mentor_id` and `starts_at`. If one
197	      exists: `ROLLBACK` and move to the next candidate.
198	   3. Under the cap? Count active bookings with this `mentor_id` and `mentor_local_date` (the class's
199	      date in the mentor's own time zone, computed with the shared time module). If the count is 2 or
200	      more: `ROLLBACK` and move to the next candidate.
201	   4. `await hooks?.beforeInsert?.()`, a test seam (see section 12).
202	   5. `INSERT` the booking, `COMMIT`, return it.
203	   6. A unique violation (`23505`) means the backstop fired: `ROLLBACK` and move to the next
204	      candidate.
205	4. If no candidate is left, return `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`.
206	
207	### Why it's safe, and the rules that keep it safe
208	
209	- **The lock covers the check and the write.** The lock is held from `FOR UPDATE` until `COMMIT` or
210	  `ROLLBACK`, so no other booking for that mentor can slip between check and insert.
211	- **One lock per transaction.** Each candidate gets its own transaction, so a request never holds two
212	  mentor locks and cannot deadlock.
213	- **Every booking write goes through `bookSlot`**, including the seed. A path that skipped the lock
214	  would bypass the turnstile.
215	- **It depends on READ COMMITTED.** Each statement takes a fresh snapshot, so T2's count after waiting
216	  sees T1's committed booking. Under REPEATABLE READ, T2 would count from a snapshot taken *before* it
217	  waited, and the cap would silently break. Don't change the isolation level; the cap race test
218	  catches it if anyone does.
219	- **The backstop.** A partial unique index on `(mentor_id, starts_at) WHERE cancelled_at IS NULL`
220	  makes a double-booked hour impossible even for code that ignores the lock. The cap has no
221	  equivalent backstop; the lock is what enforces it, and the tests prove it.
222	- **Commit first, then email.** `bookSlot` never sends email. The route handler calls `bookSlot`,
223	  responds, and sends both emails after the commit. A failed send is logged and never fails or rolls
224	  back the booking. Holding the lock while talking to SMTP would make every other booking for that
225	  mentor wait on the mail server.
226	- Plain reads (the slots list, the mentors page) take no locks and are never blocked.
227	
228	## 7. Time zones and DST
229	
230	### Rules
231	
232	1. **Instants only, in the database and on the wire.**
233	   - Postgres uses `timestamptz`.
234	   - JSON carries ISO-8601 strings ending in `Z`.
235	   - SQL never casts a `timestamptz` to a date or local time. Local dates are computed in the shared
236	     time module and stored explicitly (`mentor_local_date`).
237	2. **Zones are IANA names**, never offsets or abbreviations.
238	   - Mentors have one.
239	   - Each booking stores the parent's zone as chosen at booking time.
240	3. **In the booking rules, wall-clock time becomes an instant in exactly one place**: turning a
241	   mentor's weekly working hours into instants for a given date. Everything else goes from an instant
242	   to a local display. The one display-side exception is finding a day's local noon, which the
243	   clock-change notice uses.
244	4. **The browser groups slots into the parent's local days.** The server sends a flat list of
245	   instants; it doesn't know or care about the parent's day boundaries. Changing the zone regroups
246	   instantly, with no refetch.
247	5. **One display style for everyone, in the UI and in emails**, exactly as in the approved mockups:
248	   "Fri 23 Oct, 4:00 PM BST (London)", "9:30 PM IST (Kolkata)", "11:00 AM EST (New York)".
249	   - Dates use weekday, day and short month ("Tue 27 Oct"), plus the year on the confirmation page.
250	     Never numeric dates.
251	   - Times are 12-hour with uppercase AM/PM, as in Codeyoung's own picker.
252	   - **The abbreviation is the name people use locally.**
253	     - `Intl`'s short names depend on the locale: an `en-US` browser shows London summer time as
254	       "GMT+1". Only `en-GB` says "BST", and only `en-IN` says "IST" for India.
255	     - So take the first of `en-US`, `en-GB`, `en-IE`, `en-IN`, `en-CA`, `en-AU` whose short name
256	       isn't an offset form like `GMT+1`. If none has one, use the offset form ("GMT+9" for Tokyo).
257	     - Checked in Node: London BST/GMT, Dublin IST/GMT, Kolkata IST, New York EDT/EST, Phoenix MST,
258	       Berlin CEST/CET, St John's NDT/NST.
259	   - **The city always follows**, because abbreviations collide: "IST" is both Dublin's summer time
260	     and India's.
261	   - No locale is stored or sent anywhere. The browser's and Node's `Intl` follow the same rule.
262	6. **One clock: the app's.** Pure functions take `now` as a parameter. Only the server's clock
263	   (`createApp`'s `clock`) reads the real time. The browser takes "today" from the server's `now`,
264	   returned by `GET /api/slots` and `GET /api/mentors`, because the server filters slots with that
265	   same clock. A device clock that's a few minutes or hours wrong can't make the two disagree.
266	   - **No second clock.**
267	     - Browser code never reads its own clock (`new Date()`, `Date.now()`) for app logic.
268	     - SQL never calls `now()` in a business query. Queries take `$now` from the app clock, for
269	       example "upcoming bookings" on the mentors page.
270	     - `created_at default now()` stays, because it's an audit field and never shown.
271	   - **A stale `now` is accepted.**
272	     - The browser's `now` is a snapshot from the last response. Refetching on focus and every 60
273	       seconds keeps it within a minute.
274	     - There's no ticking clock in the browser: a minute of lag is fine for 20 parents a day.
275	     - Booking always re-checks against the server's live clock, so the worst a stale `now` can cause
276	       is a 409, never a bad booking.
277	   - **Midnight while the page is open.** When "today" moves on, the day list shifts by one. If the
278	     selected day is no longer in the list, the page falls back to the first day that has times. This
279	     is derived during render, not synced with an effect.
280	   - **No caching.** Every `/api` response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`, so a cached response can
281	     never replay an old `now`.
282	   - **The demo clock.** If `DEMO_NOW` is set to an ISO instant, the server clock starts at that
283	     instant at boot and keeps ticking: `offset = Date.parse(DEMO_NOW) - Date.now()`, then
284	     `clock = () => new Date(Date.now() + offset)`.
285	     - The seed uses the same clock. It's off by default.
286	     - While it's on, both list endpoints return `demo: true`, and the booking and mentors pages show
287	       a small banner such as "Demo clock: it's Tue 20 Oct 2026, 1:00 PM in London". A fake "today"
288	       must never mislead.
289	     - It restarts from `DEMO_NOW` whenever the app restarts, so demo time jumps back. Existing
290	       bookings stay, and the README says so.
291	     - Switching it on or off on an existing database needs `docker compose down -v` first, so the
292	       seed re-books around the new date.
293	7. **The host's time zone never matters.**
294	   - No local-time `Date` methods anywhere (`getHours`, `getDate`, `setHours`, `toLocaleString`
295	     without a `timeZone`, …). Only `getTime`, `toISOString`, `Date.UTC` and `Intl` with an explicit
296	     `timeZone`.
297	   - The time tests run three times, under `TZ=UTC`, `TZ=Pacific/Chatham` (UTC+12:45, with DST)
298	     and `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` (behind UTC, like every US parent's browser), to prove it.
299	8. **Validate zones by trying them, and require an IANA-style name.**
300	   - Try `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone })` inside a `try`. Never check membership in
301	     `Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone')`. Node's ICU still lists India as `Asia/Calcutta`, and
302	     doesn't list `Asia/Kolkata` (or `UTC`) at all. Both India names must work.
303	   - Trying alone isn't enough, because ICU also accepts abbreviations and legacy names. It maps
304	     "IST" to India, so an Irish parent's "IST" would silently become India time. It maps "EST" to a
305	     fixed UTC−5 and "GMT" to UTC. So a zone is valid only if Intl accepts it and it is either `UTC`
306	     or an `Area/Location` name (it contains a `/`).
307	
308	### The shared time module (`src/shared/time.ts`)
309	
310	No dependencies, just `Intl`. Indicative API; the builder picks the names:
311	
312	- `isValidTimeZone(tz)`
313	- `offsetMinutes(instant, tz)`: from `Intl` (`timeZoneName: 'longOffset'` or `formatToParts`).
314	- `localDate(instant, tz)`: returns `'YYYY-MM-DD'`.
315	- `zonedTimeToInstant(date, time, tz)`: wall-clock to instant, with the same disambiguation as
316	  Temporal's default (`'compatible'`):
317	  - **in a gap** (spring forward), move forward by the skipped hour: 2:00 becomes 3:00, and 2:30
318	    becomes 3:30;
319	  - **in a repeated hour** (fall back), use the first occurrence.
320	- Formatting helpers that take `(instant, tz)` and implement rule 5: the time ("4:00 PM"), the date
321	  ("Tue 27 Oct"), the abbreviation, the city, and the combined "Fri 23 Oct, 4:00 PM BST (London)".
322	  Some runtimes put a narrow no-break space (U+202F) before AM/PM, so tests normalise whitespace
323	  before comparing strings.
324	- `cityName(tz)`: the last IANA segment with `_` turned into spaces, plus a tiny alias map for cities
325	  ICU still calls by old names (`Asia/Calcutta` → Kolkata, `Europe/Kiev` → Kyiv, `Asia/Saigon` → Ho
326	  Chi Minh City).
327	
328	Mark it with `// ponytail: Intl only; swap for Temporal.ZonedDateTime once Node and Safari ship it`,
329	and the abbreviation lookup with
330	`// ponytail: six English locales cover the zones we serve; add a per-zone map if one picks a wrong name`.
331	
332	### Edge cases, with real 2026 output
333	
334	**The same mentor hour across the autumn changes.** A mentor teaching at 8:30 PM IST every weekday:
335	
336	| Mentor's 8:30 PM IST | London | New York | Phoenix |
337	|---|---|---|---|
338	| Fri 23 Oct | 4:00 PM BST | 11:00 AM EDT | 8:00 AM MST |
339	| Tue 27 Oct | 3:00 PM **GMT** | 11:00 AM EDT | 8:00 AM MST |
340	| Tue 3 Nov | 3:00 PM GMT | 10:00 AM **EST** | 8:00 AM MST |
341	
342	The class never moves for the mentor. Each parent sees it shift on their own change date. For one
343	week (25 Oct–1 Nov), London is 4 hours ahead of New York instead of 5. Phoenix never moves, because
344	Arizona doesn't observe DST.
345	
346	**The repeated hour (fall back).** On Sun 25 Oct in London, `00:00Z` is 1:00 AM BST and `01:00Z` is
347	1:00 AM GMT: two different slots with the same wall-clock label. New York does the same on Sun 1 Nov
348	(`05:00Z` is 1:00 AM EDT, `06:00Z` is 1:00 AM EST).
349	- A slot's identity is its UTC instant, never its label.
350	- On a day that mixes two offsets, every time on screen shows its abbreviation.
351	- That local day has 25 hours, and grouping by local date handles it with no special case.
352	
353	**The missing hour (spring forward).** On Sun 8 Mar 2026, New York jumped from 1:59 AM EST to
354	3:00 AM EDT, so 2:30 AM never happened. Only a mentor in a DST zone can hit this.
355	- Working hours that start inside the gap move forward by the skipped hour: 2:00 becomes 3:00, and
356	  2:30 becomes 3:30.
357	- Working hours that start in a repeated hour use its first occurrence.
358	- A window that spans a change simply has more or fewer real hours. "1:00–3:00" on the US fall-back
359	  day holds three classes; "2:00–5:00" on the spring-forward day holds two.
360	- All mentors are in India today, so this only runs in tests, which place a mentor in New York.
361	- Tests pin both 2:00 → 3:00 and 2:30 → 3:30, and the README uses exactly these two examples.
362	
363	**The parent's day vs the mentor's day.** A Los Angeles parent's Mon 26 Oct, 6:00 PM PDT is Tue 27
364	Oct, 6:30 AM IST. It shows under Monday for the parent and counts toward Tuesday for the mentor.
365	
366	**Ireland.** In the tz database's main format, Irish *winter* is marked as the daylight-saving period
367	(a negative offset change). Many runtimes ship a compatibility version that flips it back. So code
368	that reads a DST flag *can* get Ireland backwards, depending on which format of the data a library
369	uses. This design only ever asks "what's the offset at this instant?", so Dublin comes out right
370	(UTC+0 in January, UTC+1 in July; "GMT"/"IST"). Dublin has its own test.
371	
372	**Renamed zones.** Node's ICU reports India as `Asia/Calcutta`; the seed stores `Asia/Kolkata`. Both
373	must validate and format.
374	- Display goes through `cityName`, so both show "Kolkata".
375	- Comparisons between zones (for example "is the saved zone the device's zone?") compare canonical
376	  forms: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en', { timeZone }).resolvedOptions().timeZone`.
377	
378	## 8. API
379	
380	All JSON. Errors always look like `{ "error": { "code", "message", "fields"? } }`.
381	
382	| Method & path | Returns |
383	|---|---|
384	| `GET /api/slots` | `{ now, demo, slots: [{ startsAt, available }] }` for the booking window, sorted. An hour appears if at least one mentor works it. `available` is false when every such mentor is booked then or at their cap that day. |
385	| `POST /api/bookings` | Body `{ startsAt, parentName, parentEmail, childName, parentTimeZone }`. `201 { booking }`, `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `fields`, or `409 SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`. |
386	| `GET /api/bookings/:id` | `{ booking }` with the mentor's name, bio, subjects and time zone, or `404 NOT_FOUND`. The id is a random UUID, so the confirmation link can't be guessed. |
387	| `GET /api/mentors` | `{ now, demo, mentors: [{ id, name, bio, subjects, timeZone, bookings: [{ startsAt }] }] }`. Upcoming active bookings: times only, no parent or child names. |
388	
389	Validation (Zod, at the edge):
390	- **Names**: trimmed, 1–80 characters.
391	- **Email**: a valid address, at most 254 characters.
392	- **`startsAt`**: an ISO-8601 instant. It must be exactly on the UTC hour; otherwise the request fails
393	  with 400.
394	- **`parentTimeZone`**: must pass `isValidTimeZone`.
395	
396	`409 SLOT_UNAVAILABLE` covers every well-formed request for a time that can't be booked right now:
397	- every eligible mentor got taken,
398	- the time is no longer at least 2 hours away,
399	- or nobody works then.
400	
401	The client treats all of these the same way: refetch the slots and offer the nearest open times.
402	
403	Unknown errors return `500 INTERNAL` with a generic message, and the details are logged.

539	
540	```sql
541	create table mentors (
542	  id          int generated always as identity primary key,
543	  name        text not null,
544	  email       text not null unique,
545	  time_zone   text not null,          -- IANA name
546	  bio         text not null,
547	  subjects    text[] not null
548	);
549	
550	create table mentor_hours (            -- weekly working hours, in the mentor's own time zone
551	  mentor_id   int not null references mentors(id),
552	  weekday     smallint not null check (weekday between 0 and 6),  -- 0 = Sunday, like getUTCDay
553	  start_time  time not null,
554	  end_time    time not null,
555	  check (start_time < end_time)
556	);
557	
558	create table bookings (
559	  id                 uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
560	  mentor_id          int not null references mentors(id),
561	  starts_at          timestamptz not null,
562	  mentor_local_date  date not null,     -- starts_at's date in the mentor's own time zone
563	  parent_name        text not null,
564	  parent_email       text not null,
565	  child_name         text not null,
566	  parent_time_zone   text not null,
567	  class_link         text not null,
568	  created_at         timestamptz not null default now(),
569	  cancelled_at       timestamptz
570	);
571	
572	create unique index bookings_one_per_mentor_hour
573	  on bookings (mentor_id, starts_at) where cancelled_at is null;
574	create index bookings_mentor_day
575	  on bookings (mentor_id, mentor_local_date) where cancelled_at is null;
576	```

583	
584	All in Vitest. Tests that touch the database use a real Postgres (the compose `db`, separate test
585	database); no mocks for anything concurrency-related. The fixed test clock is
586	`2026-10-20T12:00:00Z`, so the 14-day window covers both autumn changes. The time tests run under
587	`TZ=UTC`, again under `TZ=Pacific/Chatham`, and again under `TZ=America/Los_Angeles`.
588	
589	**`time.test.ts`**
590	- **Offsets** across January and July: New York (−5/−4), Phoenix (−7 both), London (0/+1), Dublin
591	  (0/+1), Kolkata (+5:30), Kathmandu (+5:45).
592	- **Gap**, New York on 8 Mar 2026: 2:00 → 3:00 EDT (`07:00Z`) and 2:30 → 3:30 EDT (`07:30Z`).
593	- **Gap**, London on 29 Mar 2026: 1:30 → 2:30 BST (`01:30Z`).
594	- **Repeated hour**, first occurrence: New York, 1 Nov 2026, 1:30 → `05:30Z`; London, 25 Oct 2026,
595	  1:30 → `00:30Z`.
596	- **Local date across the date line**: Los Angeles Mon 6:00 PM is Kolkata Tue 6:30 AM.
597	- **Validation**: `isValidTimeZone` accepts `Asia/Kolkata`, `Asia/Calcutta` and `UTC`, and rejects
598	  `IST`, `EST`, `GMT` and garbage.
599	- **Formatting**: the exact rule-5 strings, with whitespace normalised:
600	  - "Tue 27 Oct, 4:00 PM GMT (London)" and "Fri 23 Oct, 4:00 PM BST (London)";
601	  - "9:30 PM IST (Kolkata)", also for `Asia/Calcutta`;
602	  - Dublin "IST" in July and "GMT" in January;
603	  - Phoenix "MST" all year;
604	  - Tokyo falling back to "GMT+9".
605	
606	**`slots.test.ts`** (pure)
607	- Weekly hours become UTC slots.
608	- The lead time and the 14-day horizon are respected.
609	- A booked hour is unavailable.
610	- A mentor at the cap loses only the other hours of *their own* day.
611	- The Los Angeles parent-day vs mentor-day case.
612	- A mentor placed in New York: 2:00–5:00 on the spring-forward day gives 2 classes, and 1:00–3:00 on
613	  the fall-back day gives 3.
614	- Grouping London's 25 Oct puts both 1:00 AM slots under that day.
615	
616	**`bookings.test.ts`** (Postgres)
617	- **Happy path**: a mentor is assigned, `starts_at` is stored as an instant, and `mentor_local_date`
618	  is in the mentor's zone. Cancelled bookings don't count toward "free" or the cap.
619	- **Same-hour race**: N concurrent bookings for one hour. Successes equal the number of eligible
620	  mentors, everyone else gets `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`, and no hour is double-booked.
621	- **Cap race, deterministic**: two concurrent bookings for different hours with the same mentor, who
622	  has one active class that day and is the only candidate. `hooks.beforeInsert` pauses 100 ms.
623	  - With the lock, the second request waits on the lock and is then rejected.
624	  - Without the lock, both pass the checks during the pause and both insert. So the test fails every
625	    time the lock is missing, not by luck.
626	  - During the build, remove the `FOR UPDATE` once and record the red run (README and transcript).
627	- **Random burst**: many concurrent bookings across random hours, then SQL checks:
628	  - no active duplicate `(mentor_id, starts_at)`;
629	  - no mentor-day with more than 2 active bookings;
630	  - every booking is inside its mentor's hours.
631	- **Backstop**: inserting a duplicate active row directly in SQL fails with `23505`. A cancelled
632	  duplicate is allowed.
633	
634	**`api.test.ts`** (supertest)
635	- Status codes and error shapes: 201, 400 with `fields`, 409, 404.
636	- `GET /api/slots` hides hours less than 2 hours away and includes full hours as `available: false`.
637	- With the mailer pointed at a dead port, a booking still returns 201 and the failure is logged.
638	- Every `/api` response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.
639	- **Demo clock**: built from `DEMO_NOW`, it starts at that instant and advances with real time. With
640	  it on, the list endpoints return `demo: true`, and both the slots and the mentors' upcoming bookings
641	  are computed from the demo `now`.
642	
643	**`email.test.ts`**: each email leads with its recipient's own time and also shows the other side's,
644	with the right abbreviations across the clock changes.
645	
646	**`booking.test.ts`** (web, pure)
647	- Grouping, the 14-day cut-off, nearest open times and days, offset-change detection.
648	- Picking the day to show: the selected day if it's still in the list, otherwise the first day with
649	  times (the midnight case).

2	
3	> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
4	
5	**Goal:** A web app where a US or UK parent books a free trial class, the system assigns an available mentor in India, and both sides see the time in their own zone. It never overbooks a mentor and never shows a misleading time.
6	
7	**Architecture:** One package and one Docker Compose stack.
8	- **Server:** Express 5 serves a small JSON API and the built React app. Postgres enforces the booking rules: a row lock per mentor plus a partial unique index.
9	- **Shared time module:** one dependency-free `Intl`-only file used by both server and browser, so the UI and the emails format time identically.
10	- **Browser:** gets a flat list of UTC instants and groups them into the parent's local days.
11	
12	**Tech Stack:**
13	- Node (server TypeScript runs via Node's type stripping), Express 5, Zod 4, `pg`, nodemailer, Postgres 17, Mailpit.
14	- React with Vite, TanStack Query, Tailwind CSS v4.
15	- Vitest and supertest.
16	
17	**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-trial-booking-design.md`. Read it first. Section numbers below (§6, §7, §10) refer to it.
18	
19	## Global Constraints
20	
21	- **Runtimes:**
22	  - Node ≥ 22.18 locally, where TypeScript type stripping is on by default.
23	  - Docker images: `node:24-alpine` and `postgres:17-alpine`, plus `axllent/mailpit:v1.31.6`.
24	- **Dependencies:**
25	  - Runtime: `express@5`, `pg`, `zod@4`, `nodemailer`.
26	  - Dev: `typescript`, `vitest`, `supertest`, `vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `react`, `react-dom`, `@tanstack/react-query`, `tailwindcss@4`, `@tailwindcss/vite`, and their `@types/*`.
27	  - Nothing else: no date library, ORM, router, component library or CSS-in-JS.
28	- **TypeScript:**
29	  - Erasable syntax only (`erasableSyntaxOnly`): no `enum`, no namespaces, no parameter properties.
30	  - Relative imports carry their `.ts`/`.tsx` extension, and type-only imports use `import type`.
31	- **Time:**
32	  - Never use local-time `Date` methods: `getHours`, `getDate`, `getDay`, `setHours`, `new Date(y, m, d)`, or `toLocaleString` without a `timeZone`.
33	  - Use `getTime`, `toISOString`, `Date.UTC`, `getUTC*` on calendar-only values, and `Intl` with an explicit `timeZone`.
34	- **One clock:**
35	  - Only `createClock` (Task 7) reads the real time. Pure functions take `now`.
36	  - SQL never calls `now()` in business queries; `created_at default now()` is the only use.
37	  - Browser code never reads the device clock for app logic.
38	- **Domain values:**
39	  - Classes are 60 minutes and start on the UTC hour.
40	  - Booking window: 120 minutes ahead at the earliest, 14 days at the latest, both ends inclusive.
41	  - Cap: 2 active bookings per mentor per calendar day in **the mentor's own time zone**. "Active" means `cancelled_at is null`.
42	- **Wording:** say "the mentor's own time zone" in code, comments and README, never "IST".
43	- **Display style everywhere** (UI and emails): `Fri 23 Oct, 4:00 PM BST (London)`, built only from `src/shared/time.ts`.
44	- **API errors:**
45	  - Shape: `{ "error": { "code", "message", "fields"? } }`.
46	  - Codes: `VALIDATION_FAILED` 400, `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE` 409, `NOT_FOUND` 404, `INTERNAL` 500.
47	  - Every `/api` response sends `Cache-Control: no-store`.
48	- **Styling:** colours, radii and the shadow come only from the `@theme` tokens in `src/web/index.css` (spec §10). No raw hex values in components.
49	- **React:**
50	  - TanStack Query for all server data, and no fetching in `useEffect`.
51	  - No `useOptimistic`, `useMemo` or `useCallback`.
52	  - `useId` for every label/input pair.
53	- **Containers:** every one sets `TZ=UTC`.
54	- **Commits:**
55	  - The whole message is lowercase, subject and body, acronyms included.
56	  - No co-authored-by or other attribution trailer.
57	  - Add files explicitly. Never commit `.playwright-mcp/`, the assignment PDF, `node_modules/` or `dist/`.
58	- **Public repository:** no secrets except the repo's own Postgres credentials, `bookings`/`bookings`.
59	- **Local database:** tests and the dev server default to `postgres://bookings:bookings@localhost:5433/bookings`, the compose `db` service on host port 5433. From Task 3 onwards, `npm test` needs `docker compose up -d db` running.
60	
61	## Review Focus
62	
63	1. **Double-clicking "Confirm"** must create one booking, not two with different mentors. The button is disabled while the booking request is pending and after it succeeds, until the page unloads (Task 11 check).
64	2. **Changing the time zone after picking a time** must keep that time selected and show the day it falls on in the new zone (Task 9 test on `shownDayKey`).
65	3. **Names that are only spaces, or contain line breaks or other control characters**, would otherwise reach email subjects. They get a 400 with field errors (Task 7 test).
66	4. **A zone that ICU spells differently from the list** (`Asia/Kolkata` vs `Asia/Calcutta`). The select must show exactly one Kolkata option, and its value must equal the current zone, or the select goes blank (Task 9 test on `zoneOptions`).
67	5. **A class that straddles a clock change.** A London class at 1:00 AM BST ends at 1:00 AM GMT, so its span must read "1:00 AM BST–1:00 AM GMT (London)", never "1:00–1:00 AM" (Task 2 test on `formatSpan`).
68	
69	## Before you start (main session, once)
70

1	# Facts the README must state (from execution)
2	
3	The build extends or departs from the spec in the places below. Each one belongs in the README, in the section that fits, stated plainly. Most go in "Assumptions and trade-offs".
4	
5	## Behaviour that goes beyond the spec's wording
6	- **Three host zones, not two.** The suite runs under `TZ=UTC`, `TZ=Pacific/Chatham` and `TZ=America/Los_Angeles`. Chatham is ahead of UTC and Los Angeles is behind it, like every US parent's browser. A local-time getter on a UTC-midnight value passes UTC and Chatham but fails Los Angeles. The spec was updated to match.
7	- **The other side's time carries its date when the days differ.** The parent's "where it's …" line and the mentor's "For the family: …" line add the date whenever the two sides fall on different calendar days, which is every US evening class. Example: "For the family: Mon 26 Oct, 5:00 PM EDT in New York". Same-day text is unchanged ("9:30 PM IST").
8	- **The 409 alert names the zone.** "Sorry, 1:00 AM BST on Sun 25 Oct is no longer available." The abbreviation tells the two 1:00 AMs apart on the clock-change day.
9	- **Body read errors are 400s.** An oversized body or an unknown `Content-Encoding` returns `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, not 500. A malformed JSON body was already a 400.
10	- **Names reject line and paragraph separators** (U+2028, U+2029) as well as control characters.
11	- **The keyboard focus ring is ink with a brand halo,** not plain brand yellow. Brand on white is 1.78:1, under WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for focus indicators.
12	
13	## Operations
14	- **Every published port is bound to `127.0.0.1`** (app 3000, Mailpit 8025 and 1025, Postgres 5433), because the database uses the well-known `bookings`/`bookings` credentials. `localhost` URLs work. To show the app from another machine, drop the `127.0.0.1:` prefix on the app port.
15	- **Fresh demo:** the seed pre-books a fully booked day and a full hour relative to the first start, and only when `bookings` is empty. On a database volume kept for a few days, the full day slides into the past. Run `docker compose down -v` before `docker compose up` for a fresh demo. That is also how to reset.
16	- **Tests in Docker:** `docker compose run --rm --build test`. The `--build` matters because the test service sits under a profile, so `up --build` never rebuilds it.
17	- The demo clock (`DEMO_NOW`) starts again from `DEMO_NOW` whenever the app restarts.
18	
19	## Known limits (honest list)
20	- The mentors page's "2 of 2 that day" badge counts upcoming bookings only, as the API returns them. On the mentor's current day, a class that has already happened isn't counted.
21	- If the server fails between committing a booking and re-reading it, the client gets a 500 for a booking that exists. The window is tiny.
22	- One app instance is assumed. Two instances starting together on an empty database could both pre-book the seed.
23	
24	## `ponytail:` notes in the code (list them under trade-offs)
25	- `src/shared/time.ts`: Intl only; swap for `Temporal.ZonedDateTime` once Node and Safari ship it.
26	- `src/shared/time.ts`: the formatter cache clears itself past 500 entries; use an LRU if real zones ever churn.
27	- `src/shared/time.ts`: six English locales pick zone abbreviations; add a per-zone map if one picks a wrong name.
28	- `src/web/booking.ts`: a one-entry cache for the zone-picker options, keyed by zone and UTC hour.
29

256	256 │ ## How bookings stay correct
257	257 │ 
258	258 │ Postgres enforces both limits. Think of a turnstile on the mentor's row: bookings for the same mentor take turns, and bookings for different mentors run in parallel.
259	259 │ 
260	260 │ ```
261	261 │ Mentor 7 already has 1 class that day. Two parents book 15:00Z and 16:00Z at once.
262	262 │ 
263	263 │ T1: lock 7 → free at 15:00? yes → 1 < 2? yes → INSERT → COMMIT (lock released)
264	264 │ T2: lock 7 → (waits for T1) → free at 16:00? yes → 2 < 2? no → ROLLBACK → try next mentor
265	265 │ ```
266	266 │ 
267	267 │ `bookSlot` in `src/server/bookings.ts`:
268	268 │ 
269	269 │ 1. The time must be on the UTC hour and inside the booking window (2 hours to 14 days ahead), or the answer is `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`.
270	270 │ 2. Candidate mentors are those whose working hours cover the whole class. They are sorted by that day's active count, then by id. This pre-check only sets the order; it is not trusted.
271	271 │ 3. For each candidate, one short transaction at `READ COMMITTED`:
272	272 │    1. `select id from mentors where id = $1 for update`: the turnstile.
273	273 │    2. Is the mentor free at that hour? If not, roll back and try the next candidate.
274	274 │    3. Is the mentor under the cap on that day in the mentor's own time zone (`mentor_local_date`)? If not, roll back and try the next candidate.
275	275 │    4. Insert the booking and commit.
276	276 │    5. A unique violation (`23505`) means the backstop fired: roll back and try the next candidate.
277	277 │ 4. If no candidate is left, the answer is `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`.
278	278 │ 
279	279 │ Why it is safe:
280	280 │ 
281	281 │ - **The lock covers the check and the write.** It is held from `for update` until commit or rollback, so no other booking for that mentor can slip in between.
282	282 │ - **One lock per transaction.** Each candidate gets its own transaction, so a request never holds two mentor locks and can't deadlock.
283	283 │ - **It depends on READ COMMITTED.** Each statement takes a fresh snapshot, so the second transaction's count, taken after it waited, sees the first one's committed booking. Under REPEATABLE READ the count would come from a snapshot taken before the wait, and the cap would silently break. `bookSlot` sets the level explicitly, and the cap race test catches a change.
284	284 │ - **The backstop.** A partial unique index on `(mentor_id, starts_at) where cancelled_at is null` makes a double-booked hour impossible even for code that skips the lock. The cap has no such backstop; the lock enforces it, and the tests prove it.
285	285 │ - **Every booking goes through `bookSlot`**, the seed included.
286	286 │ - **Commit first, then email.** `bookSlot` never sends email. The route responds, then sends both emails. A failed send is logged and never fails or rolls back the booking, and no lock is held while talking to SMTP.
287	287 │ - Plain reads (the slots list, the mentors page) take no locks and are never blocked.
288	288 │ 
289	289 │ The tests that prove it, in `src/server/bookings.test.ts`:
290	290 │ 
291	291 │ - **Same-hour race:** 10 concurrent requests for one hour with 3 free mentors make exactly 3 bookings, one per mentor.
292	292 │ - **Cap race:** a mentor with 1 class that day gets two concurrent requests for different hours. A test hook pauses 100 ms inside each transaction so they overlap. Exactly one succeeds.
293	293 │ - **Random burst:** 80 concurrent bookings over 10 mentors, then a check that no hour is double-booked, no mentor is over the cap on any of their own days, and every booking is inside working hours with the right mentor-local date.

320	320 │ ## Time zones and DST
321	321 │ 
322	322 │ All conversions and display formats live in one dependency-free file, `src/shared/time.ts`, used by both the server and the browser, so the UI and the emails format time identically.
323	323 │ 
324	324 │ - **Instants only, in the database and on the wire.** Postgres uses `timestamptz`, and JSON carries ISO-8601 strings ending in `Z`. SQL never casts a `timestamptz` to a date. The class's date in the mentor's own time zone is computed in `time.ts` and stored as `mentor_local_date`, which is what the cap counts.
325	325 │ - **Zones are IANA names**, never offsets or abbreviations. Each mentor has one, and each booking stores the parent's zone as chosen.
326	326 │ - **Wall-clock time becomes an instant in one function** in the booking rules: turning a mentor's weekly working hours into instants for a given date (`zonedTimeToInstant`). Everything else goes from an instant to a display.
327	327 │ - **The browser groups slots into the parent's local days.** The server sends a flat list of instants, so changing the zone regroups at once, with no refetch.
328	328 │ - **One display style everywhere**, in the UI and the emails: "Fri 23 Oct, 4:00 PM BST (London)", "9:30 PM IST (Kolkata)", "11:00 AM EST (New York)".
329	329 │ - **The abbreviation is the name people use there:** the first of `en-US`, `en-GB`, `en-IE`, `en-IN`, `en-CA`, `en-AU` that gives a name rather than an offset form. An `en-US` formatter calls London's summer time "GMT+1", and only `en-GB` says "BST". If no locale has a name, the offset form is used ("GMT+9" for Tokyo). The city always follows, because "IST" is both Dublin's summer time and India's.
330	330 │ - **One clock: the app's.** Only `createClock` reads the real time, and pure functions take `now`. The browser takes "today" from the `now` in each list response, so a wrong device clock can't make the page and the server disagree. SQL never calls `now()` in a business query.
331	331 │ - **The host's time zone never matters.** No local-time `Date` methods anywhere (`getHours`, `getDate`, `setHours`, `toLocaleString` without a `timeZone`). The three-zone test run checks it.
332	332 │ - **Zones are validated by trying them**, and must be `UTC` or an `Area/Location` name. Trying alone isn't enough: ICU accepts "IST" and maps it to India, and maps "EST" to a fixed UTC−5.
333	333 │ 
334	334 │ ### Edge cases, with real 2026 output
335	335 │ 
336	336 │ **The same mentor hour across the autumn changes.** A mentor teaching at 8:30 PM every weekday in Kolkata:
337	337 │ 
338	338 │ | Mentor's 8:30 PM in Kolkata | London | New York | Phoenix |
339	339 │ |---|---|---|---|
340	340 │ | Fri 23 Oct | 4:00 PM BST | 11:00 AM EDT | 8:00 AM MST |
341	341 │ | Tue 27 Oct | 3:00 PM **GMT** | 11:00 AM EDT | 8:00 AM MST |
342	342 │ | Tue 3 Nov | 3:00 PM GMT | 10:00 AM **EST** | 8:00 AM MST |
343	343 │ 
344	344 │ The class never moves for the mentor. Each parent sees it shift on their own change date. For one week (25 Oct–1 Nov), London is 4 hours ahead of New York instead of 5. Phoenix never moves, because Arizona doesn't observe DST.
345	345 │ 
346	346 │ **The repeated hour (fall back).** On Sun 25 Oct in London, `00:00Z` is 1:00 AM BST and `01:00Z` is 1:00 AM GMT: two different slots with the same wall-clock label. New York does the same on Sun 1 Nov (`05:00Z` is 1:00 AM EDT, `06:00Z` is 1:00 AM EST).
347	347 │ 
348	348 │ - A slot's identity is its UTC instant, never its label.
349	349 │ - On a day that mixes two offsets, every time on screen shows its abbreviation.
350	350 │ - That local day has 25 hours, and grouping by local date handles it with no special case.
351	351 │ - A class that straddles the change names both zones: "1:00 AM BST–1:00 AM GMT (London)".
352	352 │ 
353	353 │ **The missing hour (spring forward).** On Sun 8 Mar 2026, New York jumped from 1:59 AM EST to 3:00 AM EDT, so 2:30 AM never happened. Only a mentor in a DST zone can hit this.
354	354 │ 
355	355 │ - Working hours that start inside the gap move forward by the skipped hour: 2:00 becomes 3:00, and 2:30 becomes 3:30.
356	356 │ - Working hours that start in a repeated hour use its first occurrence.
357	357 │ - A window that spans a change simply has more or fewer real hours. "1:00–3:00" on the US fall-back day holds three classes; "2:00–5:00" on the spring-forward day holds two.
358	358 │ - All mentors are in India today, so this only runs in tests, which place a mentor in New York. The tests pin both 2:00 → 3:00 and 2:30 → 3:30.
359	359 │ 
360	360 │ This is the same rule as Temporal's default disambiguation (`'compatible'`).
361	361 │ 
362	362 │ **The parent's day vs the mentor's day.** A Los Angeles parent's Mon 26 Oct, 6:00 PM PDT is Tue 27 Oct, 6:30 AM in Kolkata. It shows under Monday for the parent and counts toward Tuesday for the mentor.
363	363 │ 
364	364 │ **Ireland.** In the tz database's main format, Irish *winter* is marked as the daylight-saving period (a negative offset change). Many runtimes ship a compatibility version that flips it back. So code that reads a DST flag can get Ireland backwards, depending on which format of the data a library uses. This app only ever asks "what's the offset at this instant?", so Dublin comes out right: UTC+0 in January and UTC+1 in July, shown as "GMT" and "IST". Dublin has its own test.
365	365 │ 
366	366 │ **Renamed zones.** Node's ICU reports India as `Asia/Calcutta`; the seed stores `Asia/Kolkata`. Both validate and both display as "Kolkata". Comparisons between zones use ICU's canonical form, so the zone picker shows exactly one Kolkata option.

368	368 │ ## Assumptions and trade-offs
369	369 │ 
370	370 │ ### Not built
371	371 │ 
372	372 │ - Accounts, login, admin screens.
373	373 │ - Cancelling or rescheduling from the app. The data model has `cancelled_at`, so only active bookings count, but there is no cancel button or endpoint.
374	374 │ - Phone or OTP verification, course or grade selection, subject-based mentor matching.
375	375 │ - Mentor time off or holiday exceptions.
376	376 │ - Calendar invites (.ics), SMS, reminders.
377	377 │ - 30-minute start times or overlapping classes.
378	378 │ - "One free trial per family" limits.
379	379 │ - Per-reader locale formatting. Everyone gets one display style.
380	380 │ - Marketing content: no pitch column, trust badges, reviews or FAQ.
381	381 │ - Guaranteed email delivery (an outbox). Email is best-effort, with no retries.
382	382 │ 
383	383 │ ### Assumptions
384	384 │ 
385	385 │ - All 10 mentors are in India (`Asia/Kolkata`), but each mentor has their own zone and every rule uses the mentor's own time zone, so a mentor elsewhere would work. The tests place one in New York.
386	386 │ - Five "UK shift" mentors teach 8:30–11:30 PM on weekdays and 2:30–6:30 PM at weekends in Kolkata. Five "US shift" mentors teach 2:30–7:30 AM in Kolkata, Sunday and Tuesday to Saturday. One mentor in each shift has a day off.
387	387 │ - The system picks the mentor: the least booked that day in their own time zone, then the lowest id.
388	388 │ - Class links are placeholders (`https://classroom.example/trial/<uuid>`).
389	389 │ 
390	390 │ ### Simplifications marked in the code (`ponytail:`)
391	391 │ 
392	392 │ - `src/shared/time.ts`: `Intl` only, no date library. The upgrade path is `Temporal.ZonedDateTime` once Node and Safari ship it.
393	393 │ - `src/shared/time.ts`: the formatter cache clears itself past 500 entries. Use an LRU if real zones ever churn.
394	394 │ - `src/shared/time.ts`: six English locales pick zone abbreviations. Add a per-zone map if one picks a wrong name.
395	395 │ - `src/web/booking.ts`: a one-entry cache for the zone-picker options, keyed by zone and UTC hour.
396	396 │ 
397	397 │ ### Where the build goes beyond the spec
398	398 │ 
399	399 │ - **The suite runs under three host zones, not two** (see [Tests](#tests)).
400	400 │ - **The other side's time carries its date when the days differ.** The parent's "where it's …" line and the mentor's "For the family: …" line add the date whenever the two sides fall on different calendar days, which is every US evening class: "For the family: Mon 26 Oct, 5:00 PM EDT in New York". Same-day text is unchanged ("9:30 PM IST").
401	401 │ - **The 409 alert names the zone:** "Sorry, 1:00 AM BST on Sun 25 Oct is no longer available." The abbreviation tells the two 1:00 AMs apart on the clock-change day.
402	402 │ - **Body read errors are 400s.** An oversized body or an unknown `Content-Encoding` returns `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, not 500. A malformed JSON body was already a 400.
403	403 │ - **Names reject line and paragraph separators** (U+2028, U+2029) as well as control characters, so they can't break an email subject.
404	404 │ - **The keyboard focus ring is ink with a brand halo,** not plain brand yellow. Brand yellow on white is 1.78:1, under the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks of focus indicators.
405	405 │ 
406	406 │ ### Known limits
407	407 │ 
408	408 │ - The mentors page's "2 of 2 that day" badge counts upcoming bookings only, as the API returns them. On the mentor's current day, a class that has already happened isn't counted.
409	409 │ - If the server fails between committing a booking and re-reading it, the client gets a 500 for a booking that exists. The window is tiny.
410	410 │ - One app instance is assumed. Two instances starting together on an empty database could both pre-book the seed.
411	411 │ 
412	412 │ ## Project layout
413	413 │ 
414	414 │ ```
415	415 │ docker-compose.yml          the stack: db, mailpit, app, and test (under a profile)
416	416 │ Dockerfile                  deps, build, test and runtime stages

421	421 │ index.html                  web entry

426	426 │   plans/2026-10-21-trial-booking.md          the implementation plan

429	429 │   types.ts                  API request and response types for server and web

433	433 │   bookings.ts               data access and the bookSlot transaction
434	434 │   slots.ts                  pure slot rules: working hours to class starts, availability, the cap
435	435 │   email.ts                  email rendering and the SMTP mailer
436	436 │   seed.ts                   10 mentors, their hours, the pre-booked classes

### Task 11: Booking page

**Files:**
- Create: `src/web/BookingPage.tsx`
- Modify: `src/web/App.tsx` (route `/` → `BookingPage`)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - `useTimeZone`, `useSlots`, `useBookSlot` (Task 10);
  - every export of `src/web/booking.ts` (Task 9);
  - the formatters (Task 2);
  - `Card`, `CardTitle`, `Progress`, `DemoBanner` (Task 10).

- [ ] **Step 1: Implement `BookingPage.tsx`** following spec §10. These decisions aren't in the spec:
  - **State**: `useReducer(flowReducer, initialFlow)`. Compute these in render, never in an effect:
    - `days = groupIntoDays(slots, timeZone, new Date(data.now))`;
    - `key = shownDayKey(…)`.
  - **Step 1 form**:
    - `required` fields, `type="email"`, `maxLength={80}`.
    - On submit, dispatch `detailsSubmitted` with trimmed values.
  - **Zone pill**:
    - The visible pill shows a globe icon, `cityName(timeZone)` and a chevron.
    - A native `<select>` covers it with `absolute inset-0 opacity-0`. It has an accessible name ("Time zone") and two optgroups, "Common" and "All time zones", built from `zoneOptions(timeZone, now)`.
    - If `!sameZone(timeZone, deviceTimeZone)`, show "Your device is set to {city} time." with a button "Use {city} time".
  - **Days and slots**:
    - Both are native radios in a `<fieldset>` with an `sr-only` legend. Each `<input class="sr-only peer">` is styled through `peer-checked:` / `peer-focus-visible:` / `peer-disabled:`.
    - Chip footer: "1 slot", "{n} slots", or "Full".
    - Arrow buttons scroll the chip row by its own width.
  - **Notices and alerts**, using the spec §10 copy:
    - The clock-change notice shows when `key >= change.dayKey`: "Clocks in {city} change on {formatDayKey(change.dayKey)}. Times from then on are {to}, not {from}." A mixed day appends "On this day each time shows its zone." and its slot labels include `zoneAbbreviation`.
    - Under the grid when any hour is full: "Greyed-out times are full: every mentor is booked then."
    - Empty day: "Every mentor is booked on {day}.", then "The nearest days with open times:" with buttons "{day} · {n} times". If there are none on either side: "No times are open in the next 14 days. Please check back soon."
    - On a 409, a `role="alert"` box: "Sorry, {time} on {date} is no longer available." and "The nearest open times are below. Pick one and confirm again. Your details are kept." It has buttons from `nearestOpenTimes`, and a label includes the date when it isn't the shown day.
  - **Confirm button**:
    - Label: "Confirm {formatDate}, {formatTime} {abbr}", or "Choose a time" when nothing is selected.
    - **Disabled while `book.isPending || book.isSuccess`**, and the label reads "Booking…". `isSuccess` covers the gap between the response and the page unloading after `location.assign`.
  - **Focus**: when the step changes, move focus to the step heading (`tabIndex={-1}`).
  - **Demo banner**: show it above the card when `data.demo`.

input.content:
# Final whole-branch review: ead9690..defd557 Reviewer: opus, read-only. I read the source tree at HEAD, the spec, the plan header and Task 11, readme-notes, final-parked and the ledger. I probed the live stack on :3000 with GET requests only (no bookings made). I ran two startup-failure checks on the host against dead targets (a dead DB port and a bad `DEMO_NOW`). I didn't rerun the suite: no specific doubt needed it, and the Task 14 gate ran 108 tests × 3 zones in Docker, with defd557 touching only the README and one comment. Counts: **Critical 0 · Important 1 · Minor 6** --- ## Strengths - **The booking transaction is the design, line for line.** In `src/server/bookings.ts:84-113`, each candidate gets its own short transaction. The isolation level is explicit (`begin isolation level read committed`, :87), the `for update` turnstile comes before both checks (:88), and the insert follows. A failed rollback can't mask the first error (:108), and a `23505` falls through to the next mentor (:109). No `pool.query` runs while a client is checked out, so the pool can't deadlock itself. pg-pool 3.14 drops broken clients on release (`!client._queryable`), so the bare `release()` is safe. - **The backstop and the cap index match the spec exactly** (`migrations/001_init.sql:32-35`). - **The cap race test can fail.** It uses a `beforeInsert` 100 ms pause (`src/server/bookings.test.ts:76-87`), and `README.md:295-318` records the red run with the `for update` removed. The ledger shows REPEATABLE READ was also checked to break the cap. - **`zonedTimeToInstant` is Temporal's 'compatible' rule in about ten lines** (`src/shared/time.ts:67-78`). Both gap cases and both repeated-hour cases are pinned (`time.test.ts:18-27`). - **`formatSpan` handles a class that straddles the change** (`time.ts:145-155`, test :64): "1:00 AM BST–1:00 AM GMT (London)". - **The whole suite runs under three host zones** (`package.json:14`), including Los Angeles. A grep finds no local-time `Date` getters, `toLocale*`, `Date.now` or `new Date()` outside `createClock`. - **There is one clock, end to end.** `createClock` validates an ISO instant with an offset (`app.ts:17-23`). The clock test uses 14 Oct, a date before any real run, so a route that read `new Date()` would fail (`api.test.ts:122-133`). The seed uses the same clock (`main.ts:13`). - **Email goes out after commit and after the response.** It uses `allSettled` plus a try/catch (`app.ts:85-92`). Tests cover a never-settling mailer and a dead SMTP port (`api.test.ts:108-120`). - **Input is validated at the edge** (`app.ts:25-32`). Names are trimmed, limited to 1–80 characters, and reject control characters and U+2028/U+2029. `startsAt` is ISO and must be on the UTC hour. Zones must be `UTC` or `Area/Location` and must pass Intl. The id is checked with `z.uuid()` before SQL (:96). All SQL is parameterised. - **The double-submit guard holds.** It has three parts: a ref guard ahead of TanStack's deferred `isPending` (`BookingPage.tsx:30,118-128`), `busy = isPending || isSuccess` (:69), and Back locked while busy (:75). The ledger records the reason. - **A zone change keeps the selected time on screen.** `shownDayKey` keeps the time selected across the change (`booking.ts:30-36`). `zoneOptions` dedupes canonically but keeps the current spelling, so Calcutta and Kolkata never blank the select (`booking.ts:80-103`). - **The seed's promises are pinned in tests for three zones** (`seed.test.ts:30-44`), including London's two 1:00 AMs under the fixed clock. The seed books only through `bookSlot` (`seed.ts:85-103`). - **Operations are careful.** Every published port binds to `127.0.0.1` (`docker-compose.yml:11,26-27,34`). The app has `init: true` (:32). The test service sits under a profile, and the runtime image has no dev dependencies. Startup failures exit with code 1. I checked this for a dead DB and for `DEMO_NOW=bogus`. - **The README matches the code** wherever I checked: the API examples, the error table, the seed hours, the demo walkthrough (the 1:00 AM GMT → Sat 24 Oct 9:00 PM EDT example is correct), the test descriptions, the race-test line number, and the env table. - **Every commit subject and body is lowercase** and carries no trailers. --- ## Issues ### Critical (Must Fix) None. I found no path to a double-booked hour, a third class in a mentor's day, a time shown without its zone, an email for an uncommitted booking, or a booking lost to an email failure. ### Important (Should Fix) **I1. A day with no bookable times reads "Full" and "Every mentor is booked on {day}."** (the known item, confirmed and sized) - **Where:** the chip footer at `src/web/BookingPage.tsx:282`, the branch at :155, and the empty-state heading at :334. The copy comes from the plan, at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-21-trial-booking.md:1425` and :1430. Those lines go back to the spec, `2026-10-20-trial-booking-design.md:445` ("A day with none says 'Full'"), which doesn't separate *no open times* from *no times at all*. So the plan and spec are at fault, not the implementer. - **Root cause:** not `groupIntoDays` (`booking.ts:16-27`). It is correct to return all 14 days (spec §10 wants 14 chips), and each `Day` already carries `slots`. The fault is that `BookingPage` labels and branches on `openCount` alone. So `slots.length === 0` (nothing offered) and "every slot unavailable" (genuinely booked out) render the same way. - **Live confirmation:** at `now = 2026-10-20T22:34Z` (11:34 PM BST), London's today is 0 open of 0 slots, so the chip shows "Full". Tapping it says "Every mentor is booked on Tue 20 Oct." Today's genuinely full days are 23 and 24 Oct (0/8 and 0/9). - **Size:** - With the seed, every US/UK local day has some working hours, so "a day nobody works" doesn't happen in this build. "Today after the 2-hour lead" happens **every day**. - On weekdays, today turns "Full" from about **7 PM EDT in New York** (the last class is 9 PM EDT) and about **9 PM BST in London**. That is prime browsing time for these parents. On Sundays in New York it reads "Full" from about 6 AM, because the last Sunday class is 8 AM EDT. - Capacity equals demand here, and the product designed "Full" as a meaningful state, so a false "every mentor is booked" misleads the reader. Nothing is booked wrongly, which is why this is Important rather than Critical. - **Smallest correct fix:** two ternaries, no new props or helpers. ```tsx // BookingPage.tsx:282, the chip footer {d.openCount ? (d.openCount === 1 ? '1 slot' : `${d.openCount} slots`) : d.slots.length ? 'Full' : 'No slots'} // BookingPage.tsx, inside EmptyDay (days[0] is today: groupIntoDays starts there) const day = days.find((d) => d.key === dayKey)!;

{day.slots.length ? `Every mentor is booked on ${formatDayKey(dayKey)}.` : dayKey === days[0]!.key ? 'No times are left today.' : `There are no times on ${formatDayKey(dayKey)}.`}

``` Keep the chip's greyed `bg-full` styling for both cases, since neither day has anything to book. Keep the "nearest days with open times" block as it is. It is exactly right for both. - **Copy:** chip footer "No slots", which matches the chip's own "1 slot / n slots". Empty state: "No times are left today." or "There are no times on {day}." Neither claims a cause, so both stay true whether the lead time ran out or nobody works that day. Spec §10 (lines 422–537) has no copy for this case. Its only related strings are the plan's "Every mentor is booked…" and `NOTHING_OPEN`. - **Also amend** spec :445 to: "A day whose times are all taken says 'Full'. A day with no times says 'No slots'." Amend plan :1425 and :1430 to match. - **Test gap:** the bug lived in JSX that no test reaches. If the wave wants a check, move the three-way label into `booking.ts` (for example `dayLabel(day)`) and add one assertion to `booking.test.ts`. That's optional. ### Minor (Nice to Have) **M1. The selected day chip and slot are barely distinguishable** (`BookingPage.tsx:278`, :316) - **What's wrong:** a selected chip is a `brand-100` fill (#FFE9AD, about 1.2:1 against the white card) with a `brand` border (1.78:1). An unselected chip has a `field` border (3.04:1), so the selected chip actually has the *weaker* outline. A selected slot is `bg-brand` (1.78:1) plus bold text. - **Why it matters:** WCAG 1.4.11 asks for 3:1 on state indicators. The slot grid's legend is `sr-only`, so for a sighted user the chip is the only on-screen marker of which day is shown. These colours come from the approved palette (spec §10), so this sits at the spec level. - **Fix:** add `peer-checked:border-ink` to both class strings (about 8:1). It keeps the look and costs one class each. **M2. Keyboard focus is lost after a 409 and misplaced after a 400** (`BookingPage.tsx:192`, :353-381, :35-39) - **After a 409:** the focused Confirm button becomes `disabled` because `selected` is cleared. Chrome then drops focus to `body`. The alternatives sit *above* Confirm in DOM order, so Tab goes nowhere useful. The `role="alert"` still announces the problem. - **After a 400:** the bounce back to step 1 focuses the "Your details" heading, not the invalid field. - **Fix:** add `autoFocus` on the first alternative button, or give the alert box `tabIndex={-1}` and focus it. On the bounce back, focus the first field with an error. **M3. Possibly stuck on "Booking…" after Back from the confirmation page** (`BookingPage.tsx:69`, `hooks.ts:36`). Unverified. - **What could happen:** `location.assign` leaves the booking page in history with `book.isSuccess` true. A browser that restores it from the back-forward cache would show a disabled "Booking…" Confirm button and a locked Back arrow until the user reloads. - **Where:** Chrome shouldn't restore it, because the page received `Cache-Control: no-store` fetch responses. Firefox and Safari may. - **Fix:** check manually once in Firefox. If it reproduces, one line in `main.tsx` fixes it: `addEventListener('pageshow', (e) => { if (e.persisted) location.reload(); });`. **M4. The email field is capped at 80 characters, while the server allows 254** (`BookingPage.tsx:234`) - **What's wrong:** `Field` applies `maxLength={80}` to all three inputs. The plan mandated this (`plan:1417`). - **Why it matters:** a long work address gets silently truncated on paste and then fails server validation. It's rare. - **Fix:** pass `maxLength={254}` for `parentEmail`. **M5. A 400 on a field the parent can't edit shows only "Some details need fixing."** (`BookingPage.tsx:185-187`) - **What's wrong:** if `parentTimeZone` fails server validation, step 2 shows only that generic sentence, and nothing on screen is fixable. This can happen when the browser's ICU knows a zone that Node's ICU doesn't. - **Fix:** show the field messages in that alert, or special-case the zone: "Please pick your time zone from the list." **M6. Nothing ignores the assignment PDF** (`.gitignore`) - **What's wrong:** `Codeyoung_Senior_Full_Stack_Engineer_Assignment (1).pdf` sits untracked in the root of a public repository. The plan forbids committing it, but nothing in git stops `git add -A` from doing so. (`.dockerignore` already excludes it.) - **Fix:** add `*.pdf` to `.gitignore`. --- ## Parked findings (final-parked.md, line by line) 1. **Formatter cache: key normalisation and a bound test.** Leave. The 500-entry clear already caps memory. Normalising only saves a few rebuilds. 2. **Task 2:** - **'UTC (UTC)':** leave. Only browsers that report UTC (privacy modes) see it, and it's cosmetic. - **'St Johns' / 'Eastern':** leave. US/UK browsers report `America/New_York`, so these names don't reach our users. - **No spring-forward span test:** leave. That span takes the same differing-offset branch the fall-back test pins. 3. **Task 3:** - **`migrate` rollback guard:** fix. It's one line, `await client.query('rollback').catch(() => {})` at `db.ts:40`, matching `bookings.ts:108` and `seed.ts:69`. Without it, a dead connection replaces the real migration error in the startup log. - **The rest:** leave. Admin pool, `drop()` re-entrancy and the concurrent-migrate test concern test helpers only, and the advisory lock is the standard pattern. Key order is cosmetic. 4. **Task 4: round-up, cross-mentor uniqueness, arrayContaining.** Leave. The NY 02:30 case covers round-up, `buildSlots` dedupes by Map key, and `arrayContaining` is enough to pin both 1:00 AMs. 5. **T5-M1 client error listener.** Already done (`db.ts:13`). Nothing to do. 6. **No regression test for the rollback guard or the error listener.** Leave. They are hard to make deterministic, both are one-liners, and both were scratch-verified. 7. **Task 6:** - **No SMTP timeouts:** leave. Sends run after the response. - **`toContain` tests:** leave. They suit multi-line bodies. - **Dead `?? name`:** leave. Harmless. - **`@types/nodemailer` shadowed:** leave, and the premise is wrong: nodemailer 10.1.7 has no `types` field, so `@types/nodemailer` is still needed. 8. **T7-M5/M6/M7: root key `''`, Zod's absent-field message, non-canonical zone case, 500 between commit and re-read.** Leave.
